title: Beyond Point Prediction: Capturing Zero-Inflated & Heavy-Tailed Spatiotemporal Data with Deep Extreme Mixture Models

problem.claim: Forecasting the intensity, frequency, and timing of extreme and non-extreme events in zero-inflated, heavy-tailed spatiotemporal data is a central modeling objective.

gap.claim: Deep-learning frameworks for these data must jointly handle zero, moderate, and extreme events, enforce mixture-component parameter constraints, and accommodate post-training changes to the extreme-event threshold.

contributions.claim: The authors propose Deep Extreme Mixture Model (DEMM), combining a deep-learning hurdle model with extreme value theory for point and distribution prediction of zero-inflated, heavy-tailed spatiotemporal variables.
DEMM allows users to set the extreme-event threshold dynamically at inference time without retraining.
The authors apply DEMM to precipitation forecasting in an extensive experimental analysis.

author_reported_evidence.claim: In precipitation forecasting experiments, the authors observe significant improvements in point and distribution prediction.

narrative_sequence.summary: Zero-inflated, heavy-tailed spatiotemporal data occurs across science and engineering applications.
Deep-learning approaches face requirements involving mixture modeling, parameter constraints, and changing extreme-event thresholds.
DEMM fuses a deep-learning hurdle model with extreme value theory for point and distribution prediction.
The framework supports changing the extreme-event threshold at inference time without retraining.
The authors evaluate DEMM for precipitation forecasting and report significant improvements in point and distribution prediction.

source_observation.claim: A model can combine a hurdle formulation with extreme value theory to represent zero, moderate, and extreme events.

interpretation.claim: Separating event regimes while modeling their distributions may better match zero-inflated and heavy-tailed targets.

application.claim: Use regime-aware probabilistic modeling when a forecasting target contains structural zeros and rare extreme values.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish performance across domains beyond the reported precipitation-forecasting application.

source_observation.claim: The framework permits the extreme-event threshold to be changed after training at inference time.

interpretation.claim: Keeping threshold selection flexible can reduce the need to retrain when the operational definition of an extreme event changes.

application.claim: Design extreme-event forecasting systems so users can adjust thresholds during deployment.

exception.claim: The abstract does not describe the computational or statistical limits of changing thresholds at inference time.

unknowns: No quantitative results, evaluation metrics, baselines, or dataset details are provided.
The abstract does not explain how mixture-component parameter constraints are implemented.
The abstract does not report results for domains beyond precipitation forecasting.
